{{nihongo|'''Nawino Shrine'''|名居神社}} is a shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined}} in Shimohinachi, {{ill|Nabari, Mie|Q166183|qid=Q166183}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}. {{nihongo|'''Nawino Shrine'''|名居神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iga Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

== History ==
Its original foundation is unknown. In the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'' (Chronicle of Empress Suiko), in {{ill|599|Q34050|qid=Q34050}} (Suiko 7), a major earthquake centered on the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamato region}} ({{ill|599 Suiko earthquake|Q17218310|qid=Q17218310}}) occurred, after which shrines for "{{ill|Nai no Kami|Q10928456|qid=Q10928456|lt=Nai no kami}}" (deity of earthquakes) were enshrined in various provinces. This is identified as the shrine in {{ill|Iga Province|Q1047128|qid=Q1047128}} among those. It is also a traditional site of {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|Q11387775|qid=Q11387775}}.

In ''[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%BC%8A%E6%B0%B4%E6%B8%A9%E6%95%85 Isui Onko]'', written in the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, Nawino Shrine is described as Una-ne-sha (former name of {{ill|Unanenofushimino Shrine|Q135039260|qid=Q135039260}})<ref>{{Cite web|title=伊水温故|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/9571119/1/189|access-date=2025-9-4}}</ref>. In the Edo period it was also called Kunitsu Daimyōjin and served as the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sōsha}} for Kunitsu shrines scattered in the upper reaches of the Hinachi River<ref>{{Cite web|title=県神社庁|url=https://jinja-net.jp/jinjacho-mie/jsearch3mie.php?jinjya=3028|access-date=2025-11-20}}</ref>.

== Remote worship sites ==
Remote worship site for Kōtaijingū [https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%81%99%E6%8B%9D-2091014 yōhai], and remote worship site for Kashihara Jingū.
